prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules, bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, redirect E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins.

statement.case_for: Round 1 did not move me off targeted protein degradation, and it moved the argument onto firmer ground. It is the only candidate that members with very different leads (Brzezinski, Linke, Chabes, Somfai, Zou, Aili) name as a preferred configuration or as an acceptable alternative, and it was the first alternative of the chair. The chemical idea is simple: a small molecule brings a protein to an E3 ligase and the cell does the rest. It has been confirmed independently for more than two decades, it opened targets once called undruggable, and the mechanism is understood in molecular detail through ternary-complex structures and the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide. A single citation can honestly span the PROTAC and glue strands, because both rest on one principle, induced proximity of a target and an E3 ligase, and the cereblon discovery is what explains why the glue strand works at all. I judge that this is a game-changing idea with real consequences, and that it is mature enough now.
statement.case_against: The attribution is imperfect and I will say so plainly. Three seats leave out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, each with a credible claim, and the first PROTACs were peptidic and cell-impermeable, so the step to drug-like degraders came from others. No PROTAC drug is approved yet, and the clinical case rests on thalidomide-class glue drugs and late-stage programmes. I also concede that the medicinal chemistry is largely modular. If the committee cannot accept a citation that joins PROTACs and glues, then the configuration is weaker than I have been presenting it.

responses.point: The chair asks whether the PROTAC strand (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon glue strand (Handa) are one discovery or two, and says a single defensible citation would move B042 above lipid nanoparticles.
responses.response: I think they are one discovery with two routes in. The shared chemical statement is that a small molecule can make an E3 ligase ubiquitinate a protein it would not normally touch. Crews and Deshaies showed it by design, and Handa showed that thalidomide and its analogues do it by accident, through cereblon. The second result explains why the first is general, and the citation I propose is written on the principle, not on the molecule class. I would add that the two-part B050 plus B052 pairing concerns me because both parts are nucleic-acid medicine, and B042 would give the committee a different kind of chemistry as a single, cleaner prize.

responses.point: Chabes says his preference for base editing would yield to B042 if base editing is judged medicine or biotechnology, and he argues the same doubt applies to degraders.
responses.response: It is a fair point that degraders are also judged through drug development, and I do not claim they escape it. The difference for me is that the chemical event is at the centre of the discovery, the formation of a ternary complex and ubiquitin transfer, and that the idea was demonstrated in the test tube and in cells before any drug existed. I accept that base editing is a defined reaction and I keep it as my first alternative. Your own willingness to move to B042 matters, because it suggests that two members who start from different places can meet there.

responses.point: Brzezinski now supports Crews, Deshaies and Handa, accepts that Deshaies has the stronger priority claim than Ciulli, and wants the expert reports to state what remains unsettled.
responses.response: I agree that the reports should state plainly what is unsettled, in particular the kinetics of ubiquitin transfer in the ternary complex and the absence of an approved PROTAC. I do not think either undermines a prize for the concept, since the committee does not need an approved drug to see that the idea has changed how targets are chosen. I welcome your conclusion on Deshaies, and I would reserve the structural and rational-design contribution of Ciulli for the discussion of the work, not the citation.

responses.point: Somfai holds that the molecules are modular medicinal chemistry, that no degrader is an established drug class, and that Crews, Deshaies, Handa and Ciulli each have claims so that no fair trio exists. He ranks B042 second to Pd C-N coupling.
responses.response: I take the point on allocation seriously, and no trio will satisfy everyone. But I would not follow the logic to the conclusion that the topic is unprizeable, because the Nobel rules already force this choice in nearly every field. The thalidomide-class glue drugs show that the drug class exists in the clinic even if PROTAC drugs do not yet. On C-N coupling, I respect the settled mechanism and the clean two-person credit, but after the 2010 prize I find the incremental principle small beside a new modality, and your own opening support was the narrowest on the shortlist.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a single citation that joins the PROTAC and molecular glue strands, and whether Handa or Ciulli should take the third seat.
Whether the current clinical record, with no approved PROTAC and glue drugs that predate the concept, is enough demonstrated consequence.
Whether a five-vote majority is reachable at all given six different lead ballots, and which of B042, B050 and B052 members who prefer other topics would actually accept.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has arisen. None of the shortlisted candidates is connected to my Warshel and EVB postdoc network, the Uppsala ribosome community or my free-energy and ligand-binding work. My simulation methods are applied to binding and catalysis, not to ubiquitin ligases or degraders, and I see no reason to recuse myself.
